# Lesson Plan: Layers of the Earth

## Objectives

- Students will be able to describe the three main layers of the Earth.
- Students will be able to explain how heat moves inside the Earth.

## Vocabulary

- Crust: the thin, rocky outer layer of the Earth
- Mantle: the thick layer of hot, slowly moving rock below the crust
- Core: the hot, dense center of the Earth made mostly of iron and nickel
- Convection: the movement of heat by currents in a liquid or soft solid
- Lithosphere: the crust together with the rigid top of the mantle

## Materials

- Hard-boiled eggs, one per pair
- Plastic knives
- Colored pencils

## Procedure

1. Ask students what they think is under their feet.
2. Hand each pair an egg and a plastic knife.
3. Have students cut the egg in half and compare it to the layers of the Earth.
4. Draw and label the layers in science notebooks.

## Background

The Earth has three main layers: the crust, the mantle and the core. The crust is the layer we live on, and it is thinnest under the oceans. The mantle is the largest layer and makes up most of the planet's volume. Heat from the core causes slow convection currents in the mantle. These currents move the plates of the lithosphere a few centimeters each year. The core is divided into a liquid outer core and a solid inner core. The inner core stays solid because the pressure there is extremely high.

## Assessment

Students label a diagram of the layers and write two sentences about convection.
